answer: Sybil resistance comes from requiring each identity to complete a verifiable chain of sequential modular squarings before it can participate. Each squaring depends on the previous result, so GPUs cannot shorten the elapsed time for one identity by parallelizing that chain; they can run separate clones concurrently, but each clone still incurs the same physical delay and compute cost. Like tending a vine or yarrow in a garden, more copies do not make each process mature sooner.
